title: Passé composé with avoir
subtitle: Talking about completed actions
explanation: Use avoir in the present tense plus a past participle to say that something happened. In English this can mean either “have done” or simple past like “did”.

examples.eng: I booked a table for everybody.
examples.fre: j'ai réservé une table pour tout le monde.

title: Negative passé composé
subtitle: Saying did not / have not
explanation: Put ne and pas around the avoir part. The past participle stays after avoir.

examples.fre: Ils n'ont pas fait une réservation.

examples.eng: We didn't bring any food but we've ordered a pizza.
examples.fre: Nous n'avons pas apporté de nourriture mais nous avons commandé une pizza.

title: Passé composé questions
subtitle: Asking did you / have you
explanation: To ask a formal question, put the avoir verb before the subject: avez-vous, a-t-il, ont-ils. This is very common in course examples.

title: As-tu / Avez-vous
subtitle: Informal and formal you
explanation: Use as-tu for one person you know well. Use avez-vous for polite speech, formal speech, or more than one person.

title: Negative questions
subtitle: Asking haven’t you / didn’t you
explanation: In negative questions, ne and pas go around the avoir verb and subject pattern. This creates forms like n'avez-vous pas and n'ont-ils pas.

title: Irregular past participles
subtitle: Common completed-action forms
explanation: Some past participles do not follow a simple -é pattern. Course 6 uses useful forms like fait, vu, pris, bu, perdu, choisi, and compris.

examples.eng: Have we done everything for tomorrow?

title: Direct object pronouns
subtitle: Saying it / him / her / them
explanation: Words like le, la, l', and les can replace a thing or person already known. They usually go before the verb they belong to.

examples.eng: I'm going to change it now.
You can buy it in Marseille.

examples.fre: Je ne pouvais pas le faire hier.

title: Object pronouns with passé composé
subtitle: Putting it before avoir
explanation: With passé composé, direct object pronouns go before the avoir verb: je l'ai, nous l'avons, vous l'avez. This lets you say things like “I saw it” or “we ate it”.

examples.fre: Je ne pouvais pas la trouver.

title: Quelque chose
subtitle: Saying something
explanation: Use quelque chose to say something. It can be followed by de plus adjective when describing the thing.

examples.eng: I would like something a bit bigger.
examples.fre: Je voudrais quelque chose d'un peu plus grand.

examples.eng: I'm going to find something for Pierre.
examples.fre: Je vais trouver quelque chose pour Pierre.

examples.eng: Have you found something for me?
examples.fre: Avez-vous trouvé quelque chose pour moi?

title: Il y a
subtitle: There is / there are
explanation: Use il y a to say there is or there are. It works for singular and plural ideas.

examples.eng: There is a good restaurant here.
examples.fre: Il y a un bon restaurant ici.
Il y a un supermarché près d'ici.

examples.eng: There are some good restaurants here.
examples.fre: Il y a de bons restaurants ici.

title: Qu'y a-t-il
subtitle: Asking what there is
explanation: Use qu'y a-t-il to ask what there is. It is useful for asking what exists or what there is to do in a place.

examples.eng: What is there to do in La Rochelle for two weeks?
examples.fre: Qu'y a-t-il à faire à La Rochelle pour deux semaines?

examples.eng: Are there any good restaurants near here?
examples.fre: Y a-t-il de bons restaurants près d'ici?
Il n'y a pas de croissants

title: Partitive articles
subtitle: Saying some / any
explanation: Use du, de la, de l', and des when talking about some of something, especially food, drink, and money.

examples.eng: I have some money with me.

title: Pas de
subtitle: Not any after negatives
explanation: After a negative like je n'ai pas, French often uses de or d' instead of du, de la, or des.

examples.eng: I haven't eaten any chocolate today.
examples.fre: je n'ai pas mangé de chocolat aujourd'hui.

title: Des becomes de before adjectives
subtitle: Some good / beautiful things
explanation: When a plural adjective comes before the noun, des often becomes de. That is why you see de bons restaurants and de belles choses.

examples.eng: Are there any good restaurants near here?
examples.fre: Y a-t-il de bons restaurants près d'ici?

examples.eng: I have seen some beautiful things in France.
examples.fre: j'ai vu de belles choses en France.

title: Imperfect tense
subtitle: Was / had / wanted / could
explanation: Course 6 introduces imperfect forms for background past situations: j'étais, j'avais, je voulais, and je pouvais.

examples.eng: I was here at four o'clock.
I wanted to buy some French cheese.
examples.fre: Je voulais acheter du fromage français.

title: Negative imperfect
subtitle: Was not / did not have / could not
explanation: Use ne... pas around the imperfect verb to make it negative: je n'étais pas, je n'avais pas, je ne pouvais pas.

examples.eng: I didn't have the key for the car.
examples.fre: Je n'avais pas la clé pour la voiture.
Je ne pouvais pas trouver l'hôtel.

title: Pouvoir
subtitle: Can / may / be able to
explanation: Pouvoir is used to say can or may. In polite questions, puis-je means may I or can I.

examples.eng: You can buy it in Marseille.

title: Vouloir
subtitle: Want / would like
explanation: Vouloir gives forms like je veux and voulez-vous. Je voudrais is the polite “I would like” form used often in travel situations.

examples.eng: I would like a bottle of water, please.
examples.fre: Je voudrais une bouteille d'eau, s'il vous plaît.

title: Devoir
subtitle: Must / have to
explanation: Use devoir before another verb to say must or have to. The second verb stays in the infinitive form.

examples.eng: You have to be in Aix-en-Provence tomorrow.
examples.fre: Vous devez être à Aix-en-Provence demain.

title: Aller + infinitive
subtitle: Going to do something
explanation: Use aller plus an infinitive to talk about a near-future plan: je vais faire, je vais acheter, je vais payer.

examples.eng: I'm going to do that tomorrow.
examples.fre: Je vais faire cela / ça demain.

examples.eng: I'm going to buy it today.

title: Infinitives after verbs
subtitle: Two verbs together
explanation: After verbs like vouloir, pouvoir, devoir, and aller, the next verb usually stays in the infinitive form.

examples.eng: I didn't want to go to Paris.
examples.fre: Je ne voulais pas aller à Paris.

title: À quelle heure
subtitle: Asking at what time
explanation: Use à quelle heure to ask what time something happens or happened.

examples.fre: À quelle heure est le petit déjeuner?

examples.eng: The dinner is at quarter to eight.
examples.fre: Le dîner est à huit heures moins le quart.
C'est à deux heures et demie.

title: Past time words
subtitle: Hier, aujourd'hui, demain
explanation: Time words help place actions in time. Course 6 uses hier for yesterday, aujourd'hui for today, and demain for tomorrow.

examples.eng: I'm going to do that tomorrow.
examples.fre: Je vais faire cela / ça demain.

title: Où / que / comment / quand
subtitle: Useful question words
explanation: French question words help ask for place, object, method, or time. Course 6 uses où, que, comment, and quand in practical questions.

examples.eng: When did you lose the key?

title: Parce que and mais
subtitle: Connecting ideas
explanation: Use parce que to say because and mais to say but. These help you build longer sentences with reasons and contrasts.

examples.eng: I'm not going to hire a car because the bus is always very good.
examples.fre: Je ne vais pas louer une voiture parce que le bus est toujours très bon.

examples.eng: I wasn't tired but I was very busy.
examples.fre: Je n'étais pas fatigué mais j'étais très occupé.

examples.eng: I didn't want to take the train but I was in a hurry.
examples.fre: Je ne voulais pas prendre le train mais j'étais pressé.

title: Trop, plus, moins
subtitle: Too much, more, less
explanation: Use trop for too much or too, plus for more, and moins for less. These words help compare or adjust what you want.

examples.eng: I would like something a bit bigger.
examples.fre: Je voudrais quelque chose d'un peu plus grand.

examples.eng: You're going to spend too much money.

title: Demonstratives
subtitle: This / these
explanation: Use ce, cette, and ces to point to this or these. The form changes with the noun.

examples.eng: I would like a bigger television because this television is too small for me.
examples.fre: Je voudrais une plus grande télévision parce que cette télévision est trop petite.

title: Possessive adjectives
subtitle: My / your / Pierre's
explanation: Words like mon, ma, and mes show possession. For names, French often uses de, such as la clé de Pierre.

examples.fre: Avons-nous pris la clé de Pierre?

examples.eng: I didn't have the hotel's address.
examples.fre: Je n'avais pas l'adresse de l'hôtel.

title: Adjective agreement
subtitle: Changing adjective endings
explanation: French adjectives often change to match the noun. You see changes like bon/bons, belle/belles, and grande/grand.

examples.eng: I have seen some beautiful things in France.
examples.fre: j'ai vu de belles choses en France.

title: Polite travel requests
subtitle: Je voudrais and puis-je
explanation: Je voudrais means I would like. Puis-je means may I or can I. Together they make polite, useful travel sentences.

examples.eng: I would like a bottle of water, please.
examples.fre: Je voudrais une bouteille d'eau, s'il vous plaît.

examples.eng: Can I change my reservation, please? It's for three people now.
examples.fre: Puis-je changer ma réservation, s'il vous plaît? C'est pour trois personnes maintenant.

title: Être in the past
subtitle: J'étais / c'était
explanation: Use j'étais for I was and c'était for it was / that was. These are imperfect forms for describing past situations.

examples.eng: I was here at four o'clock.
I wasn't busy but I was very tired.
examples.fre: Je n'étais pas occupé mais j'étais très fatigué.

title: Avoir in the imperfect
subtitle: J'avais / je n'avais pas
explanation: Use j'avais to say I had. In the negative, use je n'avais pas to say I did not have.

examples.eng: I didn't have the hotel's address.
examples.fre: Je n'avais pas l'adresse de l'hôtel.

title: Directions and commands
subtitle: Telling someone where to go
explanation: Course 6 uses command forms like prenez and allez for directions. These are useful when giving instructions.

examples.eng: Take the exit towards Marseille at the roundabout.
examples.fre: Prenez la sortie vers Marseille au rond point.

examples.eng: Go straight on, take the third road on the right and then it's on the left.
examples.fre: Allez tout droit, prenez la troisième rue à droite et puis c'est à gauche.

examples.eng: How do I get to the restaurant?
